programme.title: After Dark
programme.desc: After Dark was a British late night live discussion programme broadcast on Channel 4 television between 1987 and 1997, and on the BBC in 2003. Inspired by an Austrian programme called Club 2, Roly Keating of the BBC described it as "one of the great television talk formats of all time". In 2010 the television trade magazine Broadcast wrote "After Dark defined the first 10 years of Channel 4, just as Big Brother did for the second".

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: we cross the waters of Tauranga Moana to the island of Matakana. There, we meet the people of Oruarahi Marae and explore the rich histories of the land and their ancestor, Te Rangihouhiri. We journey back to a time when Oruarahi was thriving, tracing how the marae fell into disrepair, and hear the powerful story of its awakening and restoration — and what it took to bring the marae back to life. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: For over 100 years Mataatua wharepuni was uprooted from its home soil in Whakatāne, over 100 years in which Ngāti Awa could not be there to keep its fires burning. Ngāti Awa still mourns. Let the ancestral carvings of the house that came home arise! Arise! (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: 100 years ago, land was stolen from the tribe of Ngati-Oneone in the East Coast of New Zealand. The land was taken from them to build a port, now known as, ‘Gisborne Port.’ After years of debating to give the land back and not being heard, the decedents of Rawiri Te Eketu o te Rangi have decided to march and take occupation over the land that is rightfully theirs. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: A proud son of Ngāti Manawa, war veteran Richard Dargaville, once a soldier for the New Zealand Army, he remains forever a soldier for te ao Māori. His service reflects not just commitment to a nation, but a deep dedication to whakapapa, identity, and the ongoing struggles and strengths of his whānau and wider Māori communities. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: From haka to anthem—Te Arawa shares the stories behind powerful songs that preserve our past and move hearts worldwide. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: The life and practice of Kumeroa Gregory, a skilled rongoā and weaving practitioner. Raised in Te Urewera under the guidance of her kuia and koroua, Ruakenana, Kumeroa’s journey took a significant turn in 1970 when she moved north. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: we cross the waters of Tauranga Moana to the island of Matakana. There, we meet the people of Oruarahi Marae and explore the rich histories of the land and their ancestor, Te Rangihouhiri. We journey back to a time when Oruarahi was thriving, tracing how the marae fell into disrepair, and hear the powerful story of its awakening and restoration — and what it took to bring the marae back to life. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: We step back to honour the history of the coronation, recognising how each iwi and hapū has a unique role in shaping the beauty and strength of the Koroneihana. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: For over 100 years Mataatua wharepuni was uprooted from its home soil in Whakatāne, over 100 years in which Ngāti Awa could not be there to keep its fires burning. Ngāti Awa still mourns. Let the ancestral carvings of the house that came home arise! Arise! (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: 100 years ago, land was stolen from the tribe of Ngati-Oneone in the East Coast of New Zealand. The land was taken from them to build a port, now known as, ‘Gisborne Port.’ After years of debating to give the land back and not being heard, the decedents of Rawiri Te Eketu o te Rangi have decided to march and take occupation over the land that is rightfully theirs. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: A proud son of Ngāti Manawa, war veteran Richard Dargaville, once a soldier for the New Zealand Army, he remains forever a soldier for te ao Māori. His service reflects not just commitment to a nation, but a deep dedication to whakapapa, identity, and the ongoing struggles and strengths of his whānau and wider Māori communities. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: rage Charts
programme.desc: Australia's longest running music TV show, rage is home to the biggest vault of music videos from a diverse range of artists, genres and eras. We curate the best clips of all time to surprise and entertain you for hours.

programme.title: Dr Ann's Secret Lives
programme.desc: Dr Ann Jones ventures into the heart of Borneo's jungle to look for wild orangutan, following a team of dedicated scientists whose work is leading to new insights into one of the world's most intelligent & elusive great apes.

programme.title: Creative Types With Virginia Trioli
programme.desc: An anarchic writer, Andy Griffiths has always refused to follow the rules. He shows us into his all-important music room, and his zany 'playroom' filled with the books and toys that have fired his imagination since childhood.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce and the team head for Blair Castle, near Pitlochry in Scotland where the treasures include a chair once used by Einstein, a necklace made from stags' teeth and a rare and valuable watch with no hands.

Sarah Ferguson presents Australia's premier daily current affairs program, delivering agenda-setting public affairs journalism and interviews that hold the powerful to account. Plus political analysis from Jacob Greber.

programme.title: News Breakfast
programme.desc: Start your day informed and in front. James Glenday and Bridget Brennan bring you the latest overnight developments and the day's top stories, news with Emma Rebellato, sport with Catherine Murphy and weather with Nate Byrne.

programme.title: ABC News Mornings
programme.desc: Stay in the know with what's happening this morning. ABC News brings you up-to-the-minute news to fuel your daily conversations so you can stay connected and follow the discussion across the day. Presented by Gemma Veness.

programme.title: I Was Actually There
programme.desc: The 1997 Thredbo landslide was one of the first tragedies in Australia to unfold as a live media event, with reporters broadcasting from the mountain. After 54 hours, news broke that a sole survivor had been found alive.

programme.title: Planet America
programme.desc: Chas and John discuss the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of Nvidia, the latest on counting for the Alaska Senate seat, plus the vote and fight over Democratic leadership.

programme.title: Ages Of Ice
programme.desc: The polar seas are one of Earth's great superpowers, helping to steady the planet's climate, storing carbon, driving ocean currents and sustaining vast ecosystems. But polar oceans are getting warmer. Sea ice is disappearing.

programme.title: ABC News At Noon
programme.desc: The leading news at lunchtime. Ros Childs brings you the day's top stories and the latest news as it unfolds, with reporters in the community across Australia and around the world reporting on the issues that matter to you.

programme.title: Return To Paradise
programme.desc: When the climax of the Dolphin Cove Art Fair goes horribly wrong, an artist is stabbed to death in full view of an audience. But is the most obvious suspect, Mackenzie's Mum, actually the killer? Cast: Anna Samson, Tai Hara.

programme.title: Parliament Question Time
programme.desc: The sitting week in the Senate continues with coverage of Question Time.

programme.title: Murdoch Mysteries
programme.desc: An explosion involving the mysterious woman Watts has been investigating leads Murdoch to a surreptitious community.

programme.title: Old People's Home for 4 Year Olds
programme.desc: The seniors and teenagers participate in activities designed to help build their confidence and resilience. They learn and lean on each other, as they strengthen these vital traits and their bonds with each other deepen.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: An extraordinary double search within one family: a sister looking for her brother Keith to tell him the truth about their father, and a further search with Keith to find out more about the birth mother he never knew. (Final)

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: A second visit to Chatsworth House in Derbyshire where Fiona Bruce and the experts are kept busy as more family treasures are brought from miles around.

programme.title: Hard Quiz
